Maria K: Heads up — found a Vault token (staging-app-backup) in a partner S3 access log from last night. looks like it was emitted by an old sync job. not yet public but needs rotation ASAP.
Chris L: Ugh. where in S3? can you paste the object path?
Maria K: s3://partner-logs/redwood-ingest/2026-03-22/ingest.log.gz line ~2145, token visible after URL-encoding. I downloaded and sanitized a snippet. no external access detected yet (partner confirmed). copying sanitized excerpt: `token=***REDACTED***`
Sean P: OK. first triage: scope, blast radius, last use. Maria — can you confirm the token type (service token vs user token) and Vault path it mapped to?
Maria K: It was a Vault wrapped token that unwraps to a service identity: `svc-prod-staging-sync@infra`. Vault path `secret/data/staging/sync`. it appears to have a long TTL but the wrapper was present.
Jen H: If it's a wrapped token we need to rewrap or revoke the underlying token. Also check KMS-wrapped backups for same ciphertext.
Alex R: I'll run a quick query against Vault audit logs: `vault audit list-logs | grep staging/sync` then `vault token-lookup <token-or-uid>` — looking now.
deploy-bot: automated-scan: partner-s3-archive-scan detected potential secret-like artifact in partner-logs bucket (severity: medium). checklist created: #sec-rot-984.
Chris L: Action plan proposal: 1) revoke the underlying token and any sibling tokens 2) rotate the secret at secret/data/staging/sync (generate new secret) 3) rewrap backups in KMS and update consumers 4) RBAC check for who can create unwrap tokens 5) notify partner and schedule a 30-min maintenance window if needed.
Maria K: I agree. partner already acked and can freeze ingestion for an hour. we should not rotate the Vault root keys, only the secret and revoke tokens.
Sean P: Who will own revocation and who will push the new secret? I can do the Vault revocation (in case of TTL quirks) and Alex can push new secret values.
Alex R: I can push new secret and update configs. will need a short window to restart the sync worker. which clusters use the secret?
Maria K: staging-sync workers in cluster-staging-a and cluster-staging-b. both read from secret/data/staging/sync via the runtime auth role.
Jen H: RBAC note: ensure the runtime auth role binding doesn't allow generation of new wrapped tokens. We should run an IAM policy audit against `vault-approle-staging-sync` and reduce `wrap_create` capability if present.
Chris L: Audit logging: security-bot, can you surface all unwrap events in the last 30 days for that path and any tokens created by svc-prod-staging-sync?
security-bot: query results queued — will post when complete (ETA ~2m). includes unwrap, token-lookup, and policy-change events.
security-bot: results: 3 unwrap events in last 30d, last unwrap 2026-03-22T02:14:32Z by approle `svc-prod-staging-sync`. no policy changes detected.
Sean P: Good to know. revocation steps: `vault token-revoke -id <uid>` then rotate secret: `vault kv put secret/data/staging/sync api_key=new-key-$(date +%s)` and then re-issue short-lived tokens for consumers.
Alex R: I'll prepare a small script for rolling restart: ```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
kubectl -n staging set env deploy/sync-worker SYNC_API_KEY=$(vault kv get -field=api_key secret/data/staging/sync)
kubectl -n staging rollout restart deploy/sync-worker
```
Chris L: Add a post-rotation smoke check: hitting /health and a small synthetic sync of a sample file. if smoke fails, auto-rollback to previous secret cached in KMS.
Maria K: timeline suggestion: rotate + restart at 03:30 UTC, notify partner 30m before. I'll own partner comms and compliance notes for the incident.
Jen H: Compliance: create an evidence bundle with the audit query, the revoked token IDs, and the partner acknowledgement. I'll open an internal ticket: SEC-INC-2026-0322.
Sean P: We'll do revoke at T0. Alex will deploy new secret and restart at T0+2m. Maria will confirm partner freeze. Chris will run the RBAC audit and remove wrap_create if present. Jen will collect evidence.
Alex R: acknowledged. prepping deployment script and will standby for T0.
Maria K: one more ask — check KMS rewrap: any backups encrypted with KMS key `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/secret-ring/cryptoKeys/secret-2023`? we should rewrap those ciphertexts with a fresh key version after rotation.
Jen H: noted. I'll request key rotation and coordinate with infra team to re-encrypt archives.
security-bot: reminder: create incident label and set severity (recommended: P2) — assigned to Maria K.
Maria K: setting severity P2. running the partner freeze now. will ping when freeze confirmed. :phone:
Chris L: quick checklist for postmortem: root cause (sync job leaked wrapper), timeline, why wrapper leaked into logs (URL-encoding bug), remediation (hardening, log scrubbing, least privilege), and follow-up (wrap token policy tighten, KMS key rotation cadence).
Alex R: freeze confirmed by partner. ready on standby.
Sean P: doing revoke now. revoking token uid: `s.3Fj7...` — command output: `Success! Token revoked.`
Alex R: pulling new secret and applying to clusters. applying now.
deploy-bot: deploy started for deploy/sync-worker in cluster-staging-a and cluster-staging-b.
Alex R: rollout successful on both clusters. health checks passed. smoke sync OK.
Maria K: partner verified no further exposures. Jen, please file evidence and close SEC-INC-2026-0322 when ready.
Jen H: will do, writing notes and attaching audit logs. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Chris L: follow-up actions: 1) Log-scrub middleware for ingestion pipeline 2) enforce wrap creation policy removal for non-admin roles 3) rotate KMS key and rewrap backups 4) run org-wide scan for wrapped-token leaks. I'll create tickets.
Maria K: closing coordination thread here. great response, team.
Alex R: +1.
